tldr: Parikh et al.\textquotesingle s final Theorem 3 and Corollary 2 assert a universal no-gain equality under a known outcome shift and unknown scale. That equality is false on a common lawful Gaussian experiment: retaining both treatment-level full-mean links gives variance coefficient \(22/5<8\). The positive replacement derives the ambient original-law gradient and exact no-gain condition in a stated prospective full-overlap model. A distinct one-shared-control/global-scale companion gives the nonlocal projection applicable to the observed overlap pattern motivating the clinical example. Explicit original-record estimators attain both ambient bounds throughout the specified Lipschitz subclasses, with expected \(O(n^{-2/3})\) remainder, pointwise normal limits and 90 percent Wald coverage, including zero conditional effects.
gap: Parikh et al. link all treatment-specific full means in A.5(b) and state no gain in Theorem 3 and Corollary 2. Their application shares only BUP-NX and considers constant scale with zero shift. The observed three-cell scalar-nuisance likelihood needs a separate evaluation from the all-treatment experiment; the published comparison does not evaluate that nonlocal cost.
